verses.text: The feast of bread made without yeast, which is called the Passover, was near.
The chief priests and the teachers of the law were looking for a way to kill Jesus, because they were afraid of the people.
Then Satan entered Judas, called Iscariot, who was one of the twelve.
Judas went and discussed with the chief priests and the temple officers how he could hand Jesus over to them.
They were glad and agreed to give him money.
He agreed, and he looked for a chance to hand Jesus over when the crowd was not there.
Then the day of bread made without yeast came, the day the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed.
Jesus sent Peter and John, saying, "Go and prepare the Passover meal for us, so that we can eat it."
They asked, "Where do you want us to prepare it?"
He said, "Listen. When you enter the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him into the house he enters.
Tell the owner of the house, 'The Teacher asks you, "Where is the guest room, where I can eat the Passover with my followers?"'
He will show you a large upstairs room, already furnished. Prepare the meal there."
They went and found things just as Jesus had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
When the hour came, he sat down at the table with the twelve apostles.
He said to them, "I have very much wanted to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.
I tell you, I will not eat it again until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God."
Then he took a cup, and when he had given thanks he said, "Take this and share it among yourselves.
I tell you, I will not drink again of the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes."
He took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, "This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in memory of me."
In the same way, after supper he took the cup, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.
But look, the hand of the one who is betraying me is with me on the table.
The Son of Man will go as it has been decided, but how terrible for the man who betrays him!"
They began to ask one another which of them would do this.
They also began to argue about which of them was thought to be the greatest.
Jesus said, "The kings of the nations rule over them, and those who have power over them call themselves friends of the people.
But you must not be like that. Instead, the greatest among you should become like the youngest, and the leader should become like the one who serves.
Who is greater, the one who sits at the table, or the one who serves? Is it not the one who sits at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.
You are the ones who have stayed with me in my trials.
And I give you a kingdom, just as my Father gave one to me,
so that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom. And you will sit on thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel."
The Lord said, "Simon, Simon, listen! Satan has asked to have all of you, so that he can shake you like wheat.
But I have prayed for you, Simon, that your faith will not fail. And when you have turned back, strengthen your brothers."
Peter said, "Lord, I am ready to go with you to prison and to death!"
Jesus answered, "I tell you, Peter, the rooster will not crow today before you have said three times that you do not know me."
Then he said to them, "When I sent you out without a money bag, a bag, or sandals, did you lack anything?" "Nothing," they answered.
He said, "But now, if you have a money bag, take it, and also a bag. And if you do not have a sword, sell your coat and buy one.
I tell you, this writing must still come true in me: 'He was counted with the lawbreakers.' Yes, what is written about me is coming true."
They said, "Lord, look, here are two swords." He replied, "That is enough."
Jesus went out and made his way, as usual, to the Mount of Olives, and his followers followed him.
When he reached the place, he said to them, "Pray that you will not fall into temptation."
He withdrew from them about a stone's throw, knelt down, and prayed,
"Father, if you are willing, take this cup away from me. Yet not my will, but yours, be done."
An angel from heaven appeared to him and strengthened him.
Being in agony, he prayed even harder, and his sweat became like great drops of blood falling to the ground.
When he rose from prayer and went back to the followers, he found them asleep, worn out by sadness.
"Why are you sleeping?" he asked. "Get up and pray, so that you will not fall into temptation."
While he was still speaking, a crowd came up, and the man called Judas, one of the twelve, was leading them. He came close to Jesus to kiss him.
But Jesus asked, "Judas, are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?"
When those around Jesus saw what was about to happen, they said, "Lord, shall we strike with our swords?"
And one of them struck the high priest's servant and cut off his right ear.
But Jesus said, "No more of this!" And he touched the man's ear and healed him.
Then Jesus said to the chief priests, the temple officers, and the elders who had come for him, "Have you come out with swords and clubs, as if I were a robber?
Every day I was with you in the temple, and you did not lay a hand on me. But this is your hour, and the power of darkness."
They seized him, led him away, and took him into the high priest's house. Peter followed at a distance.
They lit a fire in the middle of the courtyard and sat down together, and Peter sat among them.
A servant girl saw him sitting there in the firelight. She looked closely at him and said, "This man was also with him."
But he denied it. "Woman, I do not know him," he said.
A little later someone else saw him and said, "You also are one of them." "Man, I am not!" Peter replied.
About an hour later, another man insisted, "Certainly this man was with him, because he is a Galilean."
Peter replied, "Man, I do not know what you are talking about!" Just as he was speaking, a rooster crowed.
The Lord turned and looked straight at Peter. Then Peter remembered the Lord's word, how he had said, "Before the rooster crows today, you will deny me three times."
And he went outside and wept bitterly.
The men who were guarding Jesus mocked him and beat him.
They blindfolded him and kept asking, "Prophesy! Who hit you?"
And they said many other insulting things to him.
At daybreak the elders of the people met together, both chief priests and teachers of the law. They led Jesus into their council
and said, "If you are the Christ, tell us." He replied, "If I tell you, you will not believe me.
And if I asked you, you would not answer.
But from now on, the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God."
They all asked, "Are you then the Son of God?" He replied, "You say that I am."
Then they said, "Why do we need any more witnesses? We ourselves have heard it from his own mouth!"
